title: Managed (cloud-hosted) environments: retire the framework's remaining local-password doors and the 'set a backup password' banner
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Found by the os-dev agent on objectstack-ai/cloud PR #4477 (the cloud card carrying the maintainer's ruling 10 on objectstack-ai/cloud#4465). Ruling 10, verbatim from that card: 「No hosted environment sets a local password for anyone, and existing owner break-glass passwords are invalidated.」 The cloud runtime now refuses password sign-in and its own `set-initial-password` twin on hosted environments. Two framework surfaces still promise a local password there.

## Measured (by reading; reach not run)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` `cloud-managed.ts`: `CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_MESSAGES.setInitialPassword` and `setUserPassword` keep a platform-admin break-glass and admit passwords on `env_native` rows on a managed environment. The full AuthPlugin's own set-initial-password door and `set-user-password` on `env_native` rows still accept a password. With hosted sign-in refusing passwords, these confer nothing, but the doors and their wording still promise a break-glass that ruling 10 removed.
2. The environment home banner "set a backup password" (cited in the cloud repo's `objectos-runtime` `backup-password-sign-in.e2e.test.ts` header, cloud#2430) now promises a password that hosted refuses.

## Change

- On a cloud-managed environment, every local-password door refuses (one stable code, one message), and the break-glass wording goes. Self-hosted keeps local passwords and local admins (ruling 10).
- The backup-password banner is not shown on a cloud-managed environment.
- The maintainer ruled stored hashes are refused, not deleted (cloud#4465 D-3): delete nothing.

Not in scope: the cloud runtime's own refusals (done in cloud PR #4477).

Carrier: objectstack. Triage sets the lane and the level.
